Heard Sri Rajendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri O.P.Mishra, learned
A.G.A. and Sri S.P. Vishwakarma, learned counsel for the informant.
2.

The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.30 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 (3) I.P.C. and 3/4 of POCSO Act and 3 (2) (5), 3 (1) W (i) of SC/ST Act, Police Station-Bansi,
District-Siddharth Nagar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Applicant before this Court is facing trial for an offence of kidnapping and rape of a minor girl and is in jail since 27.2.2021 and this application is pending for the last two years.
4.

Learned counsel for the applicant referred statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
that she on her own will accompanied the applicant and got married.
He fairly submits that he has no instructions about present status of trial as to whether statement of victim has been recorded or not.
He further submits that according to Ossification Test age of the victim on 5.3.2021 was about 16 years.
He lastly submits that in case the applicant is released on bail he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.

5. Learned A.G.A. and counsel for informant have vehemently opposed the bail application and submits that consent, if any, of a minor girl aged about 14 years is immaterial and cannot be considered to be a legal consent.
6. Learned A.G.A. further submits that he has no instructions about present status of trial.

7. I have considered the above mentioned rival submissions in referred factual and legal background and in view of established principle of jurisprudence of bail i.e 'bail is rule and jail is exception' as well as relevant factors for consideration of a bail application such as (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii) nature and gravity of the accusation; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv) danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means, position and standing of the accused;(vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being influenced; (viii) danger of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail etc. and that an order to grant or not to grant bail must assigned reasons (see Deepak Yadav Vs.
State of U.P. (2022) 8 SCC 559, Manoj Kumar Khokar Vs. State of Rajasthan and Anr (2022) 3 SCC 501, The State of Jharkhand Vs. Dhananjay Gupta @ Dhananjay Prasad Gupta: Order dated 7.11.2023 in SLP (Crl) No.10810/2023 and Shiv Kumar Vs The State of U.P. and Ors: Order dated 12.9.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.2782 of 2023), therefore, I am of considered opinion that present is not a fit case to grant bail to applicant mainly on following reasons:-
(i) Applicant is facing trial for a serious offence of kidnapping and rape of a minor girl who is just less than 16 years and in case of conviction, minimum sentence is of 20 years.

8. In the aforesaid circumstances, present bail application is rejected.

However, learned Trial Court is directed to record the statement of victim within a period of three weeks, if already not recorded and applicant will be at liberty to approach this Court of learned Trial Court as advised along with status of trial and statement of victim if recorded.
